intent: A medal-ceremony announcer: the golds, the hosts' cities, the one skier, then the population punchline.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country topped the 2026 Winter Olympics medal table?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country topped the 2026 Winter Olympics medal table?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Norway. 18 golds in Italy: the most any country has ever won at a single Winter Games.

lines.direction: ease back over the North Sea; three gold columns rise — Norway 18, USA 12, Italy 10 — the US flag-ball thinks on 'States'; the medal sticker on 'finished'
lines.text: The United States took 12 golds and 33 medals, its best ever. Italy, the hosts, 10. Norway: 41.

lines.direction: dive onto northern Italy; the Milan pin, then Cortina; on 'skier' a KLAEBO / CANADA split — 6 golds, one man, against 5 golds, one nation; the skier sticker pulses on 'Canada'
lines.text: The Games ran from Milan to Cortina. A single Norwegian skier, Johannes Klaebo, won 6 golds, more than Canada did.

lines.direction: ease back so all of Norway sits in frame; the < 6 MILLION card lands early; on 'beat' the US flag-ball slumps in and a 340 MILLION card stacks above; snowflake on 'snow'; the Norwegian flag-ball grins
lines.text: A country of under 6 million people beat a country of 340 million. Snow helps.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Small country, big winter. Follow us.
